newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Australian bond rally falters in SYCOM.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Australian bond rally falters in SYCOM.

text.p: *Australian bonds will attempt to consolidate after Friday's rally to 12-week highs faltered in SYCOM trading as strong U.S. housing data proved a set-back for U.S. Treasuries.
*Tone is expected to be cautious going into Tuesday's FOMC.
*Final wages data on Thursday seen as key local event.
Australian bond futures contracts will attempt to consolidate after Friday's rally to 12-week highs faltered in SYCOM trading as strong U.S. housing data proved a set-back for U.S. Treasuries.
The June 10-year bond futures contract ended the pre-weekend afterhours session at 92.335, down from Friday's pit close of 92.390 and 12-week peak of 92.395.

Analysts point to 92.270 as initial support before the market re-tests last week's 91.180 low which followed the Federal budget and proved to be a solid base for the subsequent 20 basis point advance.
On the upside, resistance is seen at 92.360 before the market can have another crack at 92.395 and a firmer barrier at 92.410, analysts added.

U.S. Treasuries were knocked back by a stronger than expected 2.6 percent rise in new housing starts in April and the market is expected to maintain a cautious tone going into Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting with the possibility of a policy tightening still overhanging the market.
Locally, the final wages data for the February quarter on Thursday could prove to be the key event of the week with the market keeping a keen eye on the private/public sector split.
A weak private sector outcome on wages will likely keep alive speculation of the outside possibility of a further easing which was circulating the market late last week.
The Department of Industrial Relations is also expected to release its latest report on entreprise bargaining agreements during the week.
